newsitem.title: USA: Woodbridge, N.J., rejects $145 mln school bonds.
newsitem.headline: Woodbridge, N.J., rejects $145 mln school bonds.

text.p: Voters in Woodbridge, N.J., overwhelmingly rejected a proposed $145 million school bond issue in a referendum Tuesday, the town clerk's office said Wednesday.
Of 14,757 votes, 13,307, or more than 90 percent, were cast against the plan, the clerk's office said.
The bond plan would have raised property taxes an average of $217 per year over a 30-year period for a house valued at $75,000.
The proceeds would have been used for school renovation and repair. School district officials said without the money, programs would be cut and some classes would have to be held in trailers.
